problem:
Given that $A=3I$, where $I$ is the $3\times 3$ identity matrix, which of the following statements are true?

- $4\text{det}({A}^{T})=108$
- $\text{det}(A)-6\,\text{det}(I)=0$
- $\text{det}({A}^{T})+\text{det}(A)=54$
worked_solution:
First, notice that

$$
\begin{aligned}3I & =3[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The determinant of a diagonal matrix is equal to the product of the entries on the main diagonal. Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}| & ={3}^{3}=27.\end{aligned}
$$

From the properties of determinants, we know that 

$$
\text{det}({A}^{T})=\text{det}(A)=27
$$

and

$$
\text{det}(I)=1.
$$

With that in mind, let's analyze each statement in turn.

- Statement I is true. Indeed,

$$
4\text{det}({A}^{T})=4\cdot 27=108
$$

- Statement II is false. We have

$$
\text{det}(A)-6\,\text{det}(I)=27-6\cdot 1=21\ne 0
$$

- Statement III is true. Indeed,

$$
\text{det}({A}^{T})+\text{det}(A)=27+27=54
$$

In conclusion, the correct answer is "I and III only".
